attributes.comment:
If the IRS is only send data from a filed return to FSA (as per the trainings that were given), how will FSA determine when a student or parent should have filed a return but didn't. For example, if the IRS has a W-2 for $50,000 in income but no return was filed, how will the FAFSA be processed? As a non-filer with an -3000 SAI? What about if the W-2 shows $200,000 income? Or the IRS has a 1099-INT with $20,000 of interest income?
What about if someone filed a 6 month extension and made an estimated payment but never filed their actual 1040? How will the system treat those student/parents?

My concern is that people can game the FAFSA system by filing their FAFSA before they file their tax return and therefore get a maximum Pell when they really shouldn't even receive a minimum Pell.
